edges.note: nonzero second selects flag 1 regardless of pointers and bytes
zero second with input+8 equal to third selects flag 1 without consulting bytes
zero second, pointers differ, fourth byte below third byte (unsigned) selects flag 1
zero second, pointers differ, equal bytes select flag 0 (setb needs strictly below)
zero second, pointers differ, fourth byte above third byte selects flag 0
unsigned comparison: 0xff is NOT below 0x00, so flag 0 (a signed reading would say 1)
unsigned comparison: 0x00 IS below 0xff, so flag 1 (a signed reading would say 0)
counter increment wraps mod 2**64: max counter becomes 0

rule.formula: flag = 1 if second != 0 else (1 if input+8 == third else (1 if byte[fourth+0x20] < byte[third+0x20] (unsigned) else 0)); call callee(flag, fourth, third, input+8) and ignore its result; counter at input+0x28 += 1 (mod 2**64); return fourth
rule.formula_note: the callee is called with rdi = flag, rsi = fourth (entry rcx, saved in rbp), rdx = third (entry rdx, unchanged), rcx = input+8; the return value is the fourth input (entry rcx), NOT the input struct pointer; the counter increment happens on every path, after the call
rule.inputs: input (rdi, struct pointer), second (rsi, u64), third (rdx, pointer), fourth (rcx, pointer); counter at input+0x28 (u64); flag bytes at fourth+0x20 and third+0x20
